# Add an extra life power up

## Problem statement

The AI_Hell GDD (§4.4) defines 7 power-up types (P1–P7) and a fixed 3-life per-run model with no continue mechanic. There is no way for a player to gain additional lives during a run, which limits player agency and recovery from mistakes in later levels.

## Users

- **Players** of the AI_Hell game — benefit from a high-value, rare power-up that extends their run and reduces frustration from a single mistake in later levels.
- **AI agents / human developers** implementing the game from the GDD — need the power-up specified precisely (drop rarity, stacking rule, activation) so implementations do not diverge.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want to occasionally collect an extra life drop from destroyed enemies so I can survive longer in difficult levels.
- As a **player**, I want to know extra lives are rare and capped, so the power-up feels special and doesn't trivialize the 3-life challenge.
- As a **developer**, I want the extra-life power-up defined in the GDD catalog with drop rate and cap rules so I can implement it without guesswork.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — GDD power-up catalog updated:** The power-up catalog in `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 gains a new entry **P8 – Extra Life** (collectible, passive, applies immediately), consistent with the existing P1–P7 table format (ID, name, effect, icon suggestion).
- [ ] **AC2 — Lives mechanics spec updated:** The GDD's lives mechanics (game-over/lives references) specify that collecting P8 adds **+1 life** up to a **maximum of 5 lives**; excess pickups have no effect at the cap.
- [ ] **AC3 — Drop rarity specified:** The GDD specifies that the extra-life power-up drops at a **lower rate than standard power-ups (~5% per destroyed enemy)** while standard power-ups keep their existing ~15–20% drop rate.
- [ ] **AC4 — Consistent count references:** Any GDD statements about power-up counts (e.g., "6+ distinct types" in §4.4 and the MVP content summary in §3) remain accurate with the addition (e.g., "7+ distinct types" or equivalent); the MVP "3 lives" starting value is unchanged.
- [ ] **AC5 — Validation:** The updated GDD is reviewed and accepted by the operator against the clarifying-questions appendix; the design decision (5-life cap, ~5% drop, passive) is traceable to an answered question.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation updated:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **AC7 — Test suite:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The GDD is the authoritative design artifact in this repository (no game code exists yet); the change is a documentation/design change to `docs/Game Design Document.md`.
- The GDD is a **living document** — edits are allowed and expected, tracked in the worklog.
- MVP starting lives stay at **3**; the **max cap is 5**.

## Existing state

- GDD §4.4 defines power-ups P1–P7 (P7 Dash is a permanent Space-activated core ability, distinct from temporary pickups).
- Power-ups drop from destroyed enemies with a **random chance of ~15–20% per enemy** (stated in the §4.4 intro).
- The player has **3 lives per run, no continue mechanic** (§3); game ends when out of lives (§2/game-over rules).
- No existing worklog item covers extra-life or additional power-ups.

## Desired change

Add a rare, passively collected **Extra Life** power-up (P8) to the GDD: collected by flying over it (like all pickup power-ups), instantly grants +1 life, capped at 5 lives total. It drops at a reduced rate (~5%) compared to standard power-ups. No activation key involvement (unlike P7).

## Key Files

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — **the deliverable**; update §4.4 power-up table (add P8), §4.4 intro drop-rate wording (rare exception for extra life), and any lives-mechanics / MVP-content references (§2, §3) to reflect the 5-life cap and extra-life pickup.

## Related work

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` (repository root of the design) — the document being changed; see §4.4 Power-Ups, §3 MVP content, §2 core loop.
- Work item "Game Design Document for AI_Hell" (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5) — created the GDD and its clarifying-questions appendix.
- Work item "Write the Game Design Document" (AH-0MT7QQGBU008V4R0) — implemented the GDD.
- Work item "Remove combo bonus from GDD and clarify lives model" (AH-0MT7URFNN004Z01L) — clarifies that a hit by any object removes a life; complementary to this item (extra lives restore the same pool). Both edit `docs/Game Design Document.md`; merge-order awareness needed (related-to, not blocking).
- Work item "Settle engine selection on Phaser - remove engine options B and C from GDD" (AH-0MT7UTPH3001B6IE) — unrelated to this change (engine section), surfaced by related-work scan.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** keep the change minimal — one new power-up entry plus consistent references; do not add related features (e.g., life-up stacking UI, per-life bonuses) to this item; record extras as linked work items.
- **Balance assumption:** the ~5% drop rate and 5-life cap are the operator's chosen values; if playtesting later shows imbalance, adjust via a separate work item.
- **Count-reference consistency:** updating "6+" to "7+" must not accidentally change MVP starting lives or the "3 lives" stat.
- **No code exists yet:** implementers of the eventual game must be able to derive exact behavior (instant passive +1, cap at 5) from the GDD alone.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Drop rarity — extra life is more valuable than other power-ups. Should it have a lower drop chance (e.g., ~5% per enemy) than standard power-ups?" — Answer (operator): "yes". Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Max lives cap — can extra lives stack beyond the starting 3? If so, should there be a cap (e.g., max 5)?" — Answer (operator): "max 5". Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Activation — is it collected passively with instant effect (+1 life), or needs an activation key (like P7 Dash / Space bar)?" — Answer (operator): "passive". Source: interactive reply.

# Redesign P7 Dash: make collectable teleport power-up

## Problem statement

The Game Design Document (§4.4) currently describes P7 (Dash) as a permanent, always-available ability activated by Space, unique among all power-ups in that it cannot be collected. This violates the game's design principle that all power-ups are collectables dropped by enemies, and the "dash" behavior is not what the developer wants: P7 should teleport the player instead and be renamed **Teleport**.

## Users

- **Player** — wants a movement escape tool that gets them out of danger reliably (teleport to a safe spot), rewarded via collection like every other power-up.
- **Developer/AI agent** — wants an unambiguous spec commit: P7 becomes a collectable, Space-activated teleport with safe-spot resolution and a P6 buff on arrival, so the code can be written without guessing.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want to collect a Teleport power-up from a destroyed enemy so I can press Space to escape to a safe spot in the direction I'm travelling.
- As a **player**, I want to be intangible for a moment after I reappear (P6 Phase Shift) so I am never killed at my landing spot.
- As a **developer**, I want P7 to be exactly like P1–P6 (collectable, no permanent abilities) so there is one uniform power-up model.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Collectable, not permanent:** §4.4 removes P7's "*(Space-activated, permanent)*" designation and its accompanying uniqueness note; P7 is documented as a collectable power-up dropped by enemies like P1–P6, with no always-available core ability.
- [ ] **AC2 — Teleport, not dash:** P7 is **renamed Teleport** and its effect documented as a **teleport** (not a dash): pressing Space while holding a Teleport teleports the player in the direction of travel to a **safe location** — the engine searches for the nearest safe spot (free of enemies and bullets) along the travel direction, clamped to screen bounds. If no safe spot exists in the travel direction, the player teleports to the nearest on-screen position anyway (safety guaranteed by the P6 buff, see AC4).
- [ ] **AC3 — Single-use, stackable:** Each collected P7 grants one teleport use, consumed on activation; collecting multiple P7s stacks multiple teleports (one use per collection). Priority of use is earliest-collected-first (FIFO).
- [ ] **AC4 — P6 on reappearance:** Upon reappearing after a teleport, the player gains the Phase Shift effect (intangibility, passes through enemies and bullets) for safety, as defined for P6.
- [ ] **AC5 — Docs consistency and rename:** All GDD references align with the new design — P7 is renamed **Teleport**; §2.1 controls table (Space activates the movement power-up only while held), §2.3 power-ups note, §4.4 table and note, app architecture (`Dash.ts` → `Teleport.ts`, no longer "always active"), and the controls reference in §8 (Space for dash power-up → teleport power-up).
- [ ] **AC6 — Testing/validation:** The GDD is reviewed for internal consistency (no lingering "permanent", "always active", or "dash away from nearest enemy" language); all existing documentation remains accurate.
- [ ] **AC7 — Documentation:** All related documentation updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **AC8 — Test suite:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No permanent power-ups exist in the game — P7/Teleport must conform to the existing collectable model (random drop chance ~15–20% per enemy, §4.4).
- Space remains the activation mechanism for movement-type power-ups, but it only works while the player holds at least one Teleport.
- Teleport destination must be on-screen (clamped to screen bounds) and safe (no enemies/bullets at destination).
- MVP scope unchanged (5 levels, 1 boss, 3 lives, 6+ power-ups).

## Existing state

- §2.1 controls: **Space** → "Activate movement power-up (dash/teleport away from nearest threat)".
- §2.3: "**Space bar** activates the movement-type power-up (see §4.4)".
- §4.4 table P7: **Dash** *(Space-activated, permanent)* — "Press Space to dash/teleport away from the nearest enemy in the opposite direction; 3-second cooldown".
- §4.4 note: P7 is unique — "always available… not a temporary power-up but a core ability that is always active", may be visually enhanced (e.g., Speed Boost increases dash distance).
- App architecture: `Dash.ts` — P7 (always active); controls reference §8: "Space for dash power-up".

## Desired change

- P7 renamed to **Teleport**. Collectable like P1–P6.
- Space (while a teleport is held) → teleport player in the direction of travel to the nearest safe spot, clamped to screen bounds; if no safe spot exists, teleport to nearest on-screen position anyway. Single use per collected power-up; stackable (FIFO).
- On arrival, apply P6 Phase Shift effect (intangibility ~3 seconds) to guarantee safety.
- Remove dash behavior, cooldown, "away from nearest enemy" logic, and all permanent-ability language.

## Key Files:

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §2.1 controls table (line ~32), §2.3 power-ups note (line ~46), §4.4 power-ups table + P7 note (lines ~164–167), app architecture `Dash.ts` → `Teleport.ts` (lines ~297–298), §8 controls reference (line ~468).

## Related work

- AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5 — Game Design Document for AI_Hell (source of the current P7 spec)
- AH-0MT7QQGBU008V4R0 — Write the Game Design Document
- AH-0MT7UX8LE0072MR3 — Add an extra life power up (sibling §4.4 power-up catalog edit; also touches power-up catalog)
- AH-0MT7URFNN004Z01L — Remove combo bonus from GDD and clarify lives model (sibling GDD edit)
- AH-0MT7USMWN0071UF5 — Clarify enemy pass-through and bullet-blocking rules (sibling GDD edit)
- AH-0MT7UW0Y80062NU1 — Bring simple audio effects into MVP scope (sibling GDD edit)
- AH-0MT7V5UH90023XWR — Clarify enemy health / one-hit destruction model (sibling GDD edit)
- AH-0MT7UTPH3001B6IE — Settle engine selection on Phaser (sibling GDD edit; architecture section)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "Direction of travel" means the player's current movement vector at the moment Space is pressed (last non-zero movement direction if stationary).
- **Assumption:** P6 Phase Shift applied on arrival is the full P6 effect (3-second intangibility).
- **Scope creep:** Spec additions beyond the GDD text (e.g., visual/audio teleport FX, movement-power-up UI) are out of scope and should be separate work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Activation mode — Space-activated or immediate-on-collect like P1–P5?" — Answer (user): "Yes [Space-activated]." Source: interactive reply (round 1).
- Q2: "Usage model — single use vs. time window with cooldown?" — Answer (user): "single, though the player can collect multiple teleport powerups and stack them." Source: interactive reply (round 1).
- Q3: "What is a 'safe location'?" — Answer (user): "safe spot [engine searches for nearest safe spot in the direction of travel, free of enemies/bullets, clamped to screen bounds]." Source: interactive reply (round 1).
- Q4: "Keep the name 'Dash' or rename to 'Teleport'?" — Answer (user): "rename to Teleport." Source: interactive reply (round 2).
- Q5: "Fallback when no safe spot exists in the travel direction?" — Answer (user): "teleport anyway [to nearest on-screen position, relying on the P6 buff]." Source: interactive reply (round 2).

# Add a Magnet power up

## Problem statement

The AI_Hell GDD (§4.4) defines 7 power-up types (P1–P7), all of which require the player to fly directly over the drop to collect it. There is no mechanic that helps the player gather power-ups that drift out of reach, which can make pickups feel wasted, especially during crowded bullet-hell moments.

## Users

- **Players** of the AI_Hell game — benefit from a magnet power-up that pulls nearby drops toward them, reducing the effort of collecting power-ups under fire while still requiring intentional positioning (movement or standing still).
- **AI agents / human developers** implementing the game from the GDD — need the magnet specified precisely (permanent effect, stacking behavior, attraction speed, radius) so implementations do not diverge.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want to collect a Magnet power-up so that nearby power-up drops are pulled toward my ship, making pickups easier to grab during dense bullet patterns.
- As a **player**, I want collecting multiple Magnets to increase the attraction radius, so that building up magnets feels rewarding across a run.
- As a **developer**, I want the Magnet power-up defined in the GDD catalog (permanent, stacking, radius = 2× ship size, attraction slower than ship speed) so I can implement it without guesswork.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — GDD power-up catalog updated:** The power-up catalog in `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 gains a new entry **Magnet**, consistent with the existing table format (ID, name, effect, icon suggestion), describing it as a **permanent**, passively-collected power-up.
- [ ] **AC2 — Attraction behavior specified:** The GDD specifies that the Magnet **attracts all power-up types** currently on screen (including any rare types such as Extra Life), pulling them toward the player ship.
- [ ] **AC3 — Stacking and radius specified:** The GDD specifies that collecting additional Magnets **stacks to increase the attraction radius**, with a **base radius of 2× the player ship size** and a stated per-stack radius increase (and stack cap, if capped).
- [ ] **AC4 — Speed constraint specified:** The GDD specifies that the **attraction speed is slower than the ship's movement speed**, so the player must still move toward the power-up (or remain stationary) for it to be collected; a magnet alone cannot collect a distant power-up while the ship stays put.
- [ ] **AC5 — Consistent count references:** Any GDD statements about power-up counts (e.g., "6+ distinct types" in §4.4 and the MVP content summary in §3) remain accurate with the addition.
- [ ] **AC6 — Validation:** The updated GDD is reviewed and accepted by the operator against the clarifying-questions appendix; the design decisions (permanent, all types, 2× ship-size base radius, stack rule, slower-than-ship speed) are traceable to answered questions.
- [ ] **AC7 — Documentation updated:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **AC8 — Test suite:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The GDD is the authoritative design artifact in this repository (no game code exists yet); the change is a documentation/design change to `docs/Game Design Document.md`.
- The GDD is a **living document** — edits are allowed and expected, tracked in the worklog.
- The Magnet is a **permanent** power-up (like the always-available P7 Dash concept), not a timed effect (unlike P1–P6).
- **Merge-order caution:** the sibling item "Add an extra life power up" (AH-0MT7UX8LE0072MR3) claims the **P8** slot in the same table; this item must use a non-conflicting ID (P9 or next available) and coordinate count-reference updates.

## Existing state

- GDD §4.4 defines power-ups P1–P7 (P7 Dash is a permanent Space-activated core ability; P1–P6 are temporary pickups).
- Power-ups drop from destroyed enemies with a random chance of ~15–20% per enemy.
- Power-ups are collected **by flying over them**; there is currently no attraction mechanic.
- The player ship has no fixed numeric size in the GDD — "2× ship size" is a relative unit.

## Desired change

Add a **Magnet** power-up to the GDD power-up catalog (§4.4): permanently attracts all nearby power-up drops toward the player ship. Collecting additional Magnets stacks, increasing the attraction radius; base radius is **2× the player ship size**. The attraction speed is **slower than the ship's movement speed**, so the player still needs to move toward the power-up (or at least stay still for it to drift in). It does not require an activation key.

## Key Files

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — **the deliverable**; update §4.4 power-up table (add Magnet entry), §4.4 intro count wording, and any MVP-content count references (§3) to stay consistent.

## Related work

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — the document being changed; see §4.4 Power-Ups, §3 MVP content.
- Work item "Add an extra life power up" (AH-0MT7UX8LE0072MR3) — sibling feature claiming the **P8** slot in the same table; numbering merge-order awareness needed (related-to, not blocking).
- Work item "Redesign P7 Dash: make collectable teleport power-up" (AH-0MT7UY5UR002LD5U) — in-progress sibling reworking P7 semantics; both edit §4.4 (related-to).
- Work item "Game Design Document for AI_Hell" (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5) — created the GDD and its clarifying-questions appendix.
- Work item "Write the Game Design Document" (AH-0MT7QQGBU008V4R0) — implemented the GDD.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** keep the change minimal — one new power-up entry plus consistent count references; do not add related features (e.g., magnet UI indicators, vacuum visuals, per-level balance tuning) to this item; record extras as linked work items.
- **Numbering conflict:** the sibling Extra Life item claims P8; this item should not hard-code P8 unless that sibling is closed/merged first. Recommend using the next available ID (P9) to avoid a race; coordinate via a comment on the extra life item.
- **No code exists yet:** implementers of the eventual game must be able to derive exact behavior (permanent, all power-up types, 2× ship-size base radius, stacking radius, slower-than-ship speed) from the GDD alone.
- **Balance assumption:** per-stack radius increment and any stack cap are to be chosen at planning time (sensible defaults, e.g., +50% per stack with a cap) unless the operator specifies values.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Duration/stacking model — Is Magnet a temporary timed effect (like P1–P6, where grabbing more magnets during the effect window stacks the radius), or a permanent upgrade (each pickup permanently increases the attraction radius for the rest of the run)?" — Answer (operator): "Permanent". Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Scope of attraction — Should it attract all power-up types on screen (including the rare Extra Life P8), or only standard types?" — Answer (operator): "all". Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Numbers — Any preference on base radius and per-stack radius increment, or shall I propose sensible defaults (e.g., base radius ~¼ of screen width, +50% per stack, some max)?" — Answer (operator): "base radius should be 2x the size of the ship". Source: interactive reply. Per-stack increment and cap left to planning (see Risks and assumptions).
